parsed.paper: Which Scholars Accept the Facts for the Resurrection? - Gary Habermas

core_relation.sentence: A scholarly consensus on the minimal facts for the resurrection is credible only if the scholars surveyed are genuinely informed, publish in the relevant field, and are not merely a biased Christian sample, because the same facts are acknowledged even by skeptical and liberal scholars.
core_relation.quote: So, if anything, I think I'm prejudiced, Dale. I admit it. But, I think I bend over backwards with a lot of these things and what I put in there without a comment. [S099]

product_test.quote: If if you've got a criticism, disprove it. Don't just say, "Well, I think he kind of believes like that." [S148-S149]
product_test.reason: The argument collapses entirely if the scholars are not genuinely informed or if the consensus is merely an artifact of Christian bias. Habermas treats the credibility of the minimal facts as dependent on the conjunction of (a) informed scholarly qualification, (b) publication in the field, and (c) inclusion of skeptical/liberal voices. If any one of these is missing—e.g., if the sample were only Christians or only non-publishers—the consensus claim would fail, not merely weaken.

slots.plays_role: External negentropy influx: the outside corrective that prevents the consensus from collapsing into a closed Christian echo chamber. Habermas deliberately imports hostile and liberal scholars (Bultmann, Jesus Seminar, Strauss) as an external check.
slots.quote: I do say I am slanted toward liberal scholars. [S201]

slots.plays_role: Alignment: the scholar's alignment with the data rather than with a confessional commitment. Habermas insists that even Christian scholars are 'basing their conclusions on the data.'
slots.quote: It's because even though they're Christians, they're basing their conclusions on the data. [S064]

slots.plays_role: Signal fidelity: whether the scholarly consensus is transmitted accurately despite bias and noise. Habermas checks whether critics actually read the data or just throw mud.
slots.quote: But, it's Rudolf Bultmann who says very earliest Jerusalem church. [S089]

slots.plays_role: Effective entropy: the bias, presuppositions, and methodological noise that lower the coherence of the consensus. The Jesus Seminar's presupposition 'Dead men don't rise' is treated as entropy that disqualifies their resurrection conclusions.
slots.quote: Dead men don't rise. And so for us, his life ends on Good Friday evening. [S157]

slots.plays_role: Temporal integration: the accumulation of scholarly research over decades (from 1975 onward, and back to 1941 Bultmann) that gives the consensus its weight.
slots.quote: But basically, I worked from '75 on in putting this very volume together. [S132]

slots.plays_role: Compression: the minimal facts themselves are a compressed set of six facts that distill a large body of research and can be cited across many scholars.
slots.quote: But, I can find my six facts over and over and over and over and over in James D. G. Dunn. [S039-S041]

slots.plays_role: Phase transition: the shift from a merely possible historical claim to a minimal fact occurs when a threshold of scholarly consensus is crossed. Habermas treats the empty tomb as a case that does not cross the threshold for all scholars, showing the threshold nature.
slots.quote: Because if if that was true, then the empty tomb would be a minimal fact. Not You know, if if they're all just a bunch of Christians, why on earth are Christians denying the empty tomb? [S062-S063]

slots.plays_role: Superposition: the open possibility of the resurrection remains unresolved until actualized by evidence and scholarly judgment. The Jesus Seminar closes this possibility by presupposition, which Habermas criticizes.
slots.quote: What about the resurrection? Is it not a myth pure and simple? [S109]

slots.plays_role: Non-local correlation: scholars who are otherwise independent (atheists, liberals, Christians) are correlated in their acceptance of the minimal facts, which Habermas takes as evidence that the facts are not an artifact of one community.
slots.quote: Tony Flew as far as I know when he was an atheist had no problems with the minimal facts. [S044]

slots.plays_role: Integration: the scholarly community itself, or Habermas as the integrator who assembles and weighs the evidence across the spectrum.
slots.quote: I try to go where the evidence leads. And that's my I I hope a lot of us can say that's my credo. [S139-S140]

breaks: The product test is not explicitly stated as multiplicative; Habermas often speaks as if adding more scholars (additive) strengthens the case, rather than treating each factor as necessary.

The slot Q (superposition) is weakly present: Habermas does not frame the resurrection as an unresolved possibility that remains open until actualized; he treats it as a fact to be accepted or denied.
The slot T (temporal integration) is more about the history of scholarship than about time as a constitutive factor in the truth claim.
The paper adds a factor not in the master equation: 'publication in the field' as a qualification criterion, which functions as a gatekeeping condition rather than a multiplicative factor.
extra_factors: Terminal degree and field-specific expertise as a qualification for inclusion
Publication in peer-reviewed literature as a proxy for informed opinion
parsed.one_line: Habermas's argument for the minimal facts functions as an analog to the master equation: the consensus is credible only if informed, published, and skeptical scholars all converge (multiplicative), though the paper's rhetorical structure is more additive and the slot Q is stretched.
